idiom_name: per-class Slick tables with an explicitly composed join (or JPA interop)
implementation_notes: Scala has inheritance but its data stack does not map it: Slick maps one table to a case class or tuple and Doobie is a plain SQL layer, so the joined read is composed by hand - a repository per class joins base and subtype tables, reads the discriminator and assembles the object. What replaces the classic mapper is that repository plus the explicit join, while the Java interop route (JPA/Hibernate) is the alternative that does provide the mapping. The hand-composed form is justified when the schema already has one table per class or when the application is functional-Scala through and through.
pitfalls: Slick's row shape is per table, so an inheritance hierarchy has to be flattened into explicit base/subtype row types; keeping domain case classes in the row type makes reads drift from the schema.
Nothing cascades: deleting the base row leaves subtype rows unless the foreign key says ON DELETE CASCADE or the repository deletes the path leaf-first.
